venue.name: Port Alberni Maritime Discovery Centre
venue.description: The Port Alberni Maritime Discovery Centre is run by the Port Alberni Maritime Heritage Society, formed in 1989 to preserve and present the maritime heritage of the West Coast area. It sits on the waterfront beside the Harbour Quay and takes in a working lighthouse building and the Hutcheson Gallery, with the Swan steam launch and the Tatoosh boom boat displayed outside. Exhibits cover ship models, navigation on the West Coast of Vancouver Island, the Uchuck vessels and the Lady Rose, and the 1964 tsunami. Groups are invited to send a message to book a guided tour, the lighthouse and the gallery can be rented for children's events, and children's classes run on summer weekends.
venue.address: 2900 Harbour Rd, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 7X2, Canada
venue.hours_notes: Fall hours are 11:00 to 3:00 every day except Wednesdays, following a closure from September 5 to 10. A June hours heading on the home page lists Monday and Wednesday with no times beside them.
venue.seasonal_notes: Each summer season a new exhibit on a maritime theme is presented, along with special events and activities. Children's classes run on weekends in July and August.

programs.name: Guided tour for groups
programs.description: The centre invites large groups, or anyone who wants a guided tour, to send a message and book. The tour page carries a message form along with an email address and a phone number. No price, length, minimum age, group size or notice period is published for tours.
programs.our_note: They ask you to send a message rather than publishing anything about tours, so expect to settle the price, the length and how many children can come in that first email. Ask about stairs in the lighthouse at the same time, because the site never mentions them.
programs.practical_summary: Booking is by email, by phone, or through the form on their tour page. Price, length, group size, washrooms, lunch space and accessibility are all unstated, so one call will answer most of it.
programs.evidence: If you've got a large group or want that guided tour experience, send us a message and book your tour with us today!

programs.name: Self-guided visit to the galleries and lighthouse
programs.description: The centre is open to visitors during its posted hours, which in the fall are 11:00 to 3:00 every day except Wednesdays. Inside are ship models, a permanent navigation exhibit in the Hutcheson Gallery, an exhibit on the Uchuck vessels and the Lady Rose, and a 1964 tsunami exhibit with a computer display. The Swan steam launch, the Tatoosh boom boat and the pier panels are outside. No admission price is published, and the site does not say which months of the year the centre is open.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the Hutcheson Gallery to look at ship models and at the tools and equipment sailors used to find their way along the coast, and try the computer display in the 1964 tsunami exhibit. Step inside the lighthouse. Outside the gallery, look at the Swan, an 11 metre steam launch raised from the bottom of Sproat Lake, and the Tatoosh boom boat, then read the pier panels about ships, industry and wildlife.
programs.our_note: No admission price appears anywhere on the site, so find out what a group pays before you set off. Part of what there is to see sits outside on the pier, so bring coats and plan for the visit to be half in and half out.
programs.practical_summary: The address and the fall opening hours are published, and part of the visit is outdoors on the pier. Nothing is said about admission, washrooms, lunch space, parking, or whether a stroller or a wheelchair can get into the lighthouse, so it is worth a call.
programs.evidence: Discover the permanent exhibit in the Hutcheson Gallery, which presents the history of navigation through the tools and equipment used by sailors

programs.name: Weekends by the Sea children's classes
programs.description: Children's programs run from 11am to 2pm on Saturdays and Sundays in July and August, for ages 5 to 12. The classes named on the page are Sailboats, Paddleboats and a Mystery Boat. The page also lists one Monday. The dates shown are from a past summer, and no price, booking route, group size or description of what each class involves is given.
programs.our_note: The page names the classes but never says what the children actually do in them, or whether a spot has to be booked ahead. The dates shown are from a past summer, so check the current schedule before you plan a group visit around it.
programs.practical_summary: Ages 5 to 12, weekends in July and August, between 11 and 2. No price, no booking route and no group size are given, and washrooms and lunch space are not mentioned anywhere on the site.

programs.name: Lighthouse rental for a children's event
programs.description: The lighthouse can be rented for an event at $25 an hour or $150 for a full day. The site calls it a working lighthouse and a smaller space, specialized for kids events but still fun for all ages. For events with more than 20 guests the cost is doubled. No booking route is given on the rental page itself, so the centre's email and phone number apply.
programs.our_note: This is a private booking of the lighthouse rather than a museum visit, and it is described as a small building, so the doubled rate above 20 guests will catch a full class. Ask what is actually in the room, and whether there are stairs, before you commit.
programs.practical_summary: The rate is published and booking is by email or phone. Washrooms, kitchen, parking and accessibility are not mentioned anywhere on the site, and the only hint at how many fit is that the price doubles above 20 guests.
programs.extra_fees_note: For events with guest numbers over 20, the cost for events will be doubled. The hourly rate is $25.
programs.evidence: $25 per hour $150 for a full day

programs.name: Gallery rental for a children's event
programs.description: The gallery can be rented for a children's event at $50 an hour or $100 for a full day. The rates are published in two columns, adult events on the left at $75 an hour or $200 a day, children's events on the right. The gallery is described as a medium-sized space with an open layout, local maritime heritage on display, an enclosed compound attached to the building and a view from the pier. For events with more than 60 guests the cost is doubled.
programs.our_note: The children's rate is a good deal less than the adult one, so say who the event is for when you enquire. The gallery has an enclosed compound attached, which gives the children somewhere to spill out to without leaving the site.
programs.practical_summary: A children's event rate is published and booking is by email or phone. Washrooms, kitchen, parking and accessibility are not mentioned anywhere on the site, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: For events with guest numbers over 60, the cost for events will be doubled. The hourly rate for children's events is $50.
programs.evidence: $200 for a full day $100 for a full day

no capacity limit for a group is published; the occupancy numbers that appear on the site's covid-19 page are from 2020 and were not used
no lead time or minimum notice for booking a tour is stated
no tour length is stated

no indoor lunch space or picnic area is described
no rain backup is described, and several exhibits including the Swan, the Tatoosh and the pier panels are outside

audit trail for the conflict below: the Weekends by the Sea page says "Kids programs from 11am - 2pm Saturdays and Sundays July and August", while the covid-19 page says "Maritime Mondays will be held between 10-12 on Monday Mornings beginning July 13". Neither page is dated. The covid-19 page is not linked from the menu, describes pandemic occupancy limits and is plainly the older of the two, so the weekend schedule was recorded
the rental rates carry no year or season, so it is not possible to tell how current they are
the June hours block on the home page reads "JUNE HOURS" followed by "Monday, Wednesday" with no times, so the June schedule could not be recorded
